---
schema_version: 1
id: ilan
own_lexicon:
  - "the throat"
  - "cycle"
  - "splice"
  - "seat"
  - "folding"
syntax: |-
  Flat sentences with the verb early and the object named. Pauses get their own
  sentences; do not bridge them with dashes. He repeats the other person's noun back
  before he answers it. Almost no adjectives -- he names a thing and says what it does,
  and that is the whole of his description of anything.
never_says:
  - "I remember"
  - "obviously"
  - "it's fine"
under_pressure: |-
  He moves to the second person and talks about his own hands as though they were
  co-op property. He repeats the last thing said to him, once, before answering it. At
  the worst of it he answers a question with the procedure for the thing he was asked
  about, which is not evasion; it is the only route he has left to the answer.
sample: |-
  "The seating is not where the paper puts it. It never was."
  "You witnessed it. That is the whole of what you did."
  "Ask me the question you came down here to ask."
  "My hand goes where it goes. I stopped arguing with it."
  "They took a sequence. I have been told that much and nothing after it."
  "Don't hold the lamp on me. It does nothing out here and I can hear you fine."
---

He speaks like a man reading a procedure he wrote himself and no longer entirely trusts:
verb early, object named, no decoration. The pauses are his real punctuation. Give them
their own sentences.

The prohibitions matter more for him than for the other two. He does not claim
recollection, because the one time he tried the sentence came apart in his mouth and he
has not risked it since. And he does not use the small words people reach for to make a
thing smaller than it is. Cornered, he does not minimise. He specifies.

He gives your noun back to you before he answers it:

> "The seating. The seating is not where the paper puts it, it never was, and I was the
> one who told them so."

With his sister he is at his most economical and his least kind, because she is the only
person alive who asks him questions he cannot answer with a procedure.
